newsitem.title: USA: PP&L offers compromise for pilot program.
newsitem.headline: PP&L offers compromise for pilot program.

text.p: Pennsylvania Power & Light Co said Thursday it had a compromise for a customer choice pilot program as part of the state's transition from a regulated energy marketplace to a competitive one.
As early as January 1, 1999, a third of Pennsylvanians will be able to pick the company generating their electricity.

PP&L, a unit of PP&L Resources, filed an initial plan in October as part of the deregulatory process. It developed the compromise after the Public Utilities Commission found concerns with the first plan.
PP&L said the alternative plan could cost it about $8.2 million annually. It said the plan could begin this summer and electricty would begin flowing from alternative suppliers beginning in October.
"The alternative plan we propose addresses the issues raise by the Public Utilities Commission and would avoid the need for hearings and litigation," a statement from the company said.
PP&L said its compromise offers to:
* increase average pilot credit to $0.032 per kilowatt-hour from $0.0277 per kilowatt hour;
* let pilot participants switch electricity generation suppliers on a monthly basis;
* drop certain minimum requirements and fees for electricity suppliers;
* work with the Public Utility Commission to obtain approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission for transmission rates proposed in the pilot program.
